name: Community — LTX 2.5 MSR (Multi-Subject)
author: LiconStudio
description: Put SEVERAL different people in one LTX 2.5 shot and keep each of them themselves. Licon's Multiple-Subject-Reference IC-LoRA takes up to three subject pictures plus a background and holds each one, where a single-reference model blends two people into a third who is neither. Requires a HuggingFace API key (Settings > API Keys) and one-time acceptance of the LTX 2.5 licence at https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5 - the base weights are on a gated repository. Approval is instant.

presets.name: LTX 2.5 Multi-Subject Reference
presets.tagline: Up to three people and a place, all kept apart
presets.description: Up to three subjects and a background, each held by its own reference slot.

video.displayModel: LTX 2.5 distilled (22B INT8 ConvRot) + Licon MSR V2
video.negativePrompt: blurry, distorted faces, warped hands, duplicated people, low quality

requirements.notes: Single pass - there is no latent upscaler here, so the output is sampled at the resolution you pick. Audio is generated with the video; this preset takes no audio input. The reference guide is built at 65 frames, which gives the IC-LoRA nine latent slots - enough for three subjects plus the background - and is independent of the clip length you choose. Measured 75 s for 5 s at 832x448 on a 12 GB card. Requires the ComfyUI-Licon-MSR extension, which SimpliGen installs for you at the pinned commit.

extensions.name: ComfyUI-Licon-MSR
extensions.description: Builds the multi-subject reference video the MSR IC-LoRA reads. MIT licensed; needs opencv-python, which the engine already ships.

video.description: Supply pictures of up to three subjects plus a background plate. Name them in the prompt as 'Image 1', 'Image 2' and 'Image 3' and say what each one does - that labelling is how the model tells them apart. The background slot is literal: it uses the room you give it, so describe the action in the prompt rather than the place. Keep every subject at a similar depth and describe them side by side. Identity holds well for three standing figures, but a subject placed further back gets fewer pixels and reads less clearly - and wording like 'behind a drum kit' tends to put that person behind the OTHER PLAYERS rather than behind their instrument.
